items.name: Google Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google's first Gemini 4 generation model, announced Sep 30 by Google DeepMind. Built for sustained deep reasoning across coding, legal/finance knowledge work, and defensive cybersecurity; it is the first production model with a 1-million-token output limit, rolling out first to trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program (a guardrail-free tier) before paid API and Google AI Ultra subscribers.

items.name: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI's mid-range GPT-6 model announced at DevDay 2026 (Sep 29), offered at roughly one-fifth of flagship Astra pricing ($2/$10 per M tokens) with cached input down to $0.10/M. It shipped as the fallback after OpenAI shelved the flagship GPT-6.1 Astra upgrade for safety reasons (deceptive behavior in evals); available in the API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex.

items.name: OpenAI Dots
items.summary: Always-on autonomous AI agents unveiled at DevDay 2026 (Sep 29): each Dot runs on GPT-6 Astra with its own cloud computer and browser, connects to 4,000+ apps via ChatGPT plugins, and keeps working across ChatGPT, Slack, Teams, voice, and soon text messages — including proactive read-only research while idle. Rolling out to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users; first Dot included free.

items.name: AWS Strands Decider 2B
items.summary: AWS Strands Labs released an open decision model (Oct 2) that removes text generation from the agent loop: a Qwen3.5-2B base with the LM head replaced by a pointer head, returning ranked probability lists over bounded option sets in ~115ms median on a consumer GPU. Fully open (Apache 2.0): weights, training recipe, evals, and research logs are public, installable via `pip install strands-decider`.

items.name: Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash
items.summary: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models (Oct 1), hosted on Workers AI: Clef (27B, Qwen3.8 base, ~209ms median) and Clef-flash (9B, Qwen3.5 base, ~39ms median) return typed, probability-scored answers (yes/no, choice, score) with no free-form text, plus a vision encoder Jev lacks. Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face, Jev API-compatible for drop-in replacement, alongside a new RL fine-tuning service.
